A.explanation: Resultant force is zero because opposite $F$ pairs cancel, but equilibrium also needs zero resultant torque, which is not satisfied here.

B.explanation: Resultant force is not $4F$ because the two horizontal $F$ forces oppose each other and the two vertical $F$ forces oppose each other.

C.explanation: Resultant torque is not zero because all four tangential forces of magnitude $F$ tend to turn the disc in the same clockwise sense.

D.explanation: Resultant force is zero but the four torques add to $2Fd$ clockwise, so the disc has angular acceleration and is not in equilibrium.

hints: Notice the directions at the four tangent points: top $F$ to the right versus bottom $F$ to the left, and left $F$ up versus right $F$ down.
Recall equilibrium needs both zero resultant force and zero resultant torque, so check force cancellation and then moment sense separately.
Take moments about the centre where each $F$ has perpendicular distance $d/2$ and check whether the four $F \times d/2$ moments oppose or add.
walkthrough: Resolve forces: horizontal $F$ right + $F$ left = 0 and vertical $F$ up + $F$ down = 0, so resultant force $= 0$.
Recall torque about the centre is $F \times$ perpendicular distance, here radius $= d/2$ for each tangential force.
Determine sense: each force tends to rotate the disc clockwise, so none cancel.
Add magnitudes: total torque $= 4 \times F \times d/2 = 2Fd$.
Equilibrium requires zero force and zero torque, so zero force alone is insufficient. This is option D.
